content_blocks.title: Example: Context and Resource Management Best Practices
content_blocks.code:
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "net/http"
    "net/http/httptest"
    "strings"
)

func main() {
    handler := http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { fmt.Fprintln(w, "ok") })
    req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/health", nil)
    rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
    handler.ServeHTTP(rec, req)
    fmt.Println(rec.Code, strings.TrimSpace(rec.Body.String()))
}
content_blocks.run_instructions: Save as main.go and run `go run main.go`. httptest avoids opening a network port for this isolated handler example.

task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates propagating context or a closely related concept.
Inputs, relevant state changes, and expected output are clear.
At least one boundary case is deliberately tested or documented.
Errors are handled honestly and no success state is reported when the operation fails.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming the happy-path output proves all inputs are safe.
common_mistakes.why: Empty, malformed, boundary, or concurrent cases may follow different paths.
common_mistakes.fix: Add focused tests for a normal input and at least one relevant edge case.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring returned errors or external-system status.
common_mistakes.why: Go APIs commonly report expected failures as explicit error values.
common_mistakes.fix: Check errors close to the operation, add useful context when propagating, and clean up resources.

common_mistakes.problem: Using an API or syntax without checking the selected Go version.
common_mistakes.why: Language and standard-library capabilities can change between releases.
common_mistakes.fix: Record `go version`, inspect the `go` directive, and read official release notes for version-specific topics.

summary: Context and Resource Management Best Practices provides a reusable rule or workflow for Go programs.

Prefer a small reproducible example, explicit errors, appropriate tests, and version-matched official documentation.
